## Soft Metadata

> [!WARNING]
> **Tier 2 (community estimate)** — Soft Metadata below adapted from SAGE publisher pages and domain knowledge of qualitative health research editorial culture (Morse / Charmaz / grounded theory legacy). Submission practitioners are invited to upgrade individual claims to Tier 1 via `/ja-validate`. See [SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md](../../../../SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md) for the Skeleton → Tier 2 → Tier 1 lifecycle.

> **The core value of this entry.** OpenAlex cannot fill any of these — they require lived experience and community knowledge. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidance.

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Very High — international qualitative health research authorship |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | High — indigenous health knowledge welcomed |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | Very High — health disparities, marginalized populations |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Qualitative health research — grounded theory (Morse, Charmaz), phenomenological health research, narrative health research, critical / decolonial qualitative health |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must demonstrate **rigorous qualitative health research** with methodological transparency, sustained reflexive engagement, theoretical / conceptual development.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Pure quantitative redirected to Health Psychology or SSM.

### Methodological Preferences

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 0 | Outside scope |
| Qualitative interviews | 5 | Core — IPA, narrative, phenomenological |
| Autoethnography | 4 | Health-autoethnographic welcomed |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 4 | Welcomed |
| Mixed methods | 3 | With qualitative dominance |
| Meta-analysis | 1 | Qualitative meta-synthesis welcomed |
| Grounded theory | 5 | Distinctive strength |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |

Reviewers from qualitative health research community — SAGE qualitative family + IIQM (International Institute for Qualitative Methodology). Common demands: "Methodological transparency?", "Reflexive engagement?", "Theoretical contribution?".

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Quantitative-only health submissions
- AI use without disclosure per SAGE policy
- Insufficient methodological transparency

### Soft Tax

Low for qualitative health tradition authors. Sustained reflexive engagement expected.

### Best Suited For

- Illness narrative qualitative research
- Chronic illness lived experience studies
- Health disparities qualitative work
- End-of-life / palliative care qualitative
- Mental health qualitative
- Caregiving research
- Decolonial health research

### Not Recommended For

- Pure quantitative health (consider Health Psychology, SSM)
- Mixed-methods with quant dominance
- Authors unfamiliar with qualitative methodology

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Qualitative Inquiry](./qualitative-inquiry.md) | Closest SAGE qualitative peer; broader scope |
| 2 | [Qualitative Research in Psychology](./qualitative-research-in-psychology.md) | T&F qualitative-psychology peer |
| 3 | [Health Psychology](../psychology/health-psychology.md) | If reframed as mixed-methods with quant scaffolding |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from Health Psychology as "too qualitative," QHR is the SAGE qualitative-health home.
